_note: From svdbench/standalone/{solvers,primitives,divide_conquer,iterative}.py and svdlab/recipes.py at main (2026-10-30). All standalone solvers first scale A by max|a_ij|; wide inputs are transposed. 'Jacobi SVD' = one-sided Hestenes Jacobi with round-robin parallel ordering (all n/2 disjoint pairs per round, n-1 rounds per sweep), tol 10*eps, stop when max normalized off-diagonal correlation <= tol. 'Jacobi eigh' = two-sided Hermitian Jacobi, same ordering. Householder QR / bidiag / tridiag are column-by-column Python loops of rank-1 reflector updates (no blocking).

blocks.svd:bidiag_qr.steps: Householder bidiagonalization (A = Q B P^H) -> implicit-shift bidiagonal QR (bdsqr, Givens chasing, lock-step batched) -> U = Q Ub, V = P Vb
blocks.svd:bidiag_qr.iterative: yes: bdsqr QR iterations until superdiagonal deflates (tol 10*eps, max_iter 60n); count = bdsqr_iterations

blocks.svd:bidiag_dc.steps: Householder bidiagonalization -> recursive divide-and-conquer bidiagonal SVD in float64 (split, recurse, rank-one secular-equation merge by bisection; leaves n<=4 and hard merges solved by one-sided Jacobi)
blocks.svd:bidiag_dc.iterative: yes: bisection inside each merge + Jacobi on leaves/refinements (max_sweeps 80); recursion depth ~log2(n/4)

blocks.svd:jacobi.steps: one-sided Jacobi on A directly, round-robin cyclic sweeps; s = column norms, U = W/s
blocks.svd:jacobi.iterative: yes: sweeps until off <= 10*eps (max_sweeps 60); count = jacobi_sweeps

blocks.svd:block_jacobi.steps: block one-sided Jacobi: columns grouped in blocks of 4, round-robin over block pairs, each pair (8 columns) orthogonalized by inner one-sided Jacobi SVD; convergence test on full Gram correlation
blocks.svd:block_jacobi.iterative: yes: outer block sweeps (max 30, tol 40*eps) x inner Jacobi sweeps per block pair

blocks.svd:qr.steps: Householder QR (A = QR) -> one-sided Jacobi SVD of R (n x n) -> U = Q Ur

blocks.svd:tsqr.steps: tall-skinny QR (row tiles of 4n rows, binary reduction tree; for square/small m it is a single Householder QR) -> one-sided Jacobi SVD of R -> U = Q Ur

blocks.svd:gram_jacobi.steps: G = A^H A -> two-sided Jacobi eigendecomposition of G -> s = sqrt(eig), U = A V / s (null columns completed)
blocks.svd:gram_jacobi.iterative: yes: Hermitian Jacobi sweeps (max 60); count = eigen_sweeps
blocks.svd:gram_jacobi.rank: full (values below eps*n*lambda_max discarded/zeroed; squares the condition number)

blocks.svd:gram_dc.steps: G = A^H A -> Householder tridiagonalization -> Cuppen divide-and-conquer tridiagonal eigensolver (float64 merges, leaves n<=4 by Jacobi eigh) -> s = sqrt(eig), U = A V / s
blocks.svd:gram_dc.iterative: yes: bisection in merges + leaf Jacobi

blocks.svd:polar_qdwh.steps: normalize by ||A||_F -> QDWH polar iteration (dynamically weighted Halley; Cholesky + two triangular solves per step, or QR of [sqrt(c)X; I] when c>100) -> H = Up^H A -> Jacobi eigh of H -> U = Up V
blocks.svd:polar_qdwh.iterative: yes: polar iterations until ||X_{k+1}-X_k||_max <= 10*eps (max 40, typically ~6) + Jacobi eigh sweeps

blocks.svd:polar_newton_schulz.steps: normalize by ||A||_F -> Newton-Schulz polar iteration X <- X(3I - X^H X)/2 (GEMM only) -> H = Up^H A -> Jacobi eigh -> U = Up V
blocks.svd:polar_newton_schulz.iterative: yes: polar iterations (max 120, tol 10*eps); slow for small sigma_min/||A||_F + eigen sweeps

blocks.svd:polar_halley.steps: normalize -> Halley polar iteration (a,b,c)=(3,1,3), Cholesky-based inverse per step -> H = Up^H A -> Jacobi eigh -> U = Up V

blocks.svd:polar_polynomial.steps: normalize -> 5th-order polynomial polar iteration X(15I - 10G + 3G^2)/8, G = X^H X (GEMM only) -> H -> Jacobi eigh -> U

blocks.svd:polar_cans.steps: normalize -> CANS polar iteration: odd minimax polynomial of order 3 (Remez coefficients recomputed every step from bounds [1-e,1+e]) applied by GEMMs -> H -> Jacobi eigh -> U
blocks.svd:polar_cans.iterative: yes: polar iterations (max 120) + Remez + eigen sweeps

blocks.svd:randomized.steps: Halko-Martinsson-Tropp: Omega Gaussian (n x l, l = min(rank+8, n)), Q = qr(A Omega), 2 power iterations (QR each half step) -> Jacobi SVD of Q^H A -> U = Q Ub
blocks.svd:randomized.iterative: fixed 2 power iterations + Jacobi sweeps on the small matrix
blocks.svd:randomized.rank: truncated (rank parameter); with rank=n it is a full SVD of Q^H A

blocks.svd:subspace.steps: same as randomized (subspace iteration with QR re-orthonormalization)

blocks.svd:block_krylov.steps: randomized block Krylov: keep all power-iteration blocks [Q0, Q1, Q2] (each reorthogonalized twice against previous), QR of concatenation -> Jacobi SVD of Q^H A
blocks.svd:block_krylov.iterative: fixed iterations=2 (stops early when Krylov basis fills m columns) + Jacobi sweeps

blocks.svd:lanczos.steps: Golub-Kahan-Lanczos bidiagonalization with full reorthogonalization (steps = min(m,n, 2*rank+8)) -> recompute core Ub^H A Vb -> Jacobi SVD of the core
blocks.svd:lanczos.iterative: fixed `steps` Lanczos steps + Jacobi sweeps on core

recipes.golub_kahan.steps: blocks.bidiagonalize (Householder) -> blocks.bidiagonal_svd (bdsqr) -> U = Q Ub, V = P Vb; same pipeline as bidiag_qr but through the recipe API

recipes.randomized.steps: HMT via blocks: sketch A Omega (rank+8 cols), 2 power iterations with blocks.qr, blocks.jacobi_svd(Q^H A)

recipes.lanczos.steps: blocks.lanczos_bidiagonalize (GKL, full reorth, steps = min(m,n,2*rank+8)) -> blocks.bidiagonal_svd (bdsqr on the Lanczos bidiagonal) -> U = U_L Ub

recipes.jacobi.steps: identical to blocks.svd:jacobi (blocks.jacobi_svd) - not benchmarked separately
